title: Hestia: An Efficient Cross-Level Debugger for High-Level Synthesis
problem: High-level synthesis (HLS) compilers are complex black-box procedures lacking transparency, creating a semantic gap between software descriptions and RTL implementations. Existing debugging methods are either too slow (RTL simulation) or too abstract (software-level simulation) to effectively debug HLS-generated hardware.
motivation: Efficient and transparent debugging is critical for making HLS a practical design methodology for hardware development.
method: Hestia implements a multi-level interpreter that enables debugging HLS designs at different abstraction levels, from software to RTL. It maintains equivalent mappings across abstraction levels to bridge the semantic gap and facilitate bug identification and localization. The tool provides breakpoints and stepping facilities at multiple granularities, reducing both hardware details exposure and debugging time.
key_novelty: A cross-level debugging approach that maintains semantic equivalence mappings between software and hardware abstractions to enable efficient HLS debugging without excessive RTL simulation details.
contributions: Multi-level interpreter architecture for debugging HLS designs across different abstraction levels
Cross-level semantic mapping mechanism to bridge the software-to-RTL gap
Flexible breakpoint and stepping facilities at multiple granularities
Demonstrated significant simulation speedup and improved debugging capability with validation
